findingsAndCorrections.summary: Root cause: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/ingest-existing.js's ingestAtomsOntoRecords/ENTITY_TYPE_TO_RAIL mapping already correctly maps building-footprint atoms to the buildingFootprint rail, but had zero callers in any job in this repo -- a wired mechanism that reports as built because the code exists, but nothing ever runs it, same doctrinal shape as several other findings this program has caught this sprint (doc-repo-26's review named this precisely: the same shape as the setbackFrontFt allowlist entry with no writer behind it, and the same shape as a constraint-index builder that made a different feature refuse for every user while its own close read as honest -- 'the artifact is correct, the close is truthful, and no customer is served'). Fixed with a new job, src/jobs/parcel-building-footprint-reconcile.mjs, that feeds the vendored function (unmodified -- ENGINE_PIN.json honored) real atoms via a body->>'parcelNodeId' AS entity_id alias (atoms.entity_id itself carries a volatile ':footprint:<slot>' suffix and cannot be the join key directly -- resolves the integration lane's 2026-09-06 open question between 'never built' and 'key-grammar mismatch': both were true and compound), and handles absence atoms with a new job-level function (the vendored companionRows helper can only ever emit kind:'value' for a companion rail). Live-smoke-verified against real Bastrop atoms: real footprints, absence atoms, and a nonexistent parcel all resolved correctly. PLAIN STATEMENT, not a footnote: this has NOT been run with --apply against production. parcel_record_cell.buildingFootprint is 100% unaccounted for all six CTX counties as of this close, identically to before this lane started, including Caldwell's 35,269 real atoms. The mechanism is proven; the rail is not yet populated. See 'What remains open' for the named, owned follow-up that would close that gap.

The dispatch's framing ('no writer ever built') was stale. A real writer exists (hauska-engine packages/engine-core/scripts/write-setback-city.mjs + src/setback-writer/plan-city-setback.ts, PR #366/#367, merged 2026-08-31, live on hauska-engine main), city-scoped to Bastrop/Elgin, with its apply path explicitly and deliberately held (SETBACK_APPLY_HELD, unchanged since Aug 31). More load-bearing: the operator's ACTIVE ruling (_decisions/2026-09-05_f11_setback_pe_table_port_and_live_bastrop_fetch.md, status: active) explicitly rejected routing F-11 through hauska-factory's atom-ingestion/ledger path -- that exact plan was proposed and stood down the same day (_decisions/2026-09-05_f11_setback_bastrop_elgin_atom_reuse.md, superseded). Real setback service now goes directly to Property Explorer's own runtime, bypassing parcel_record_cell for this rail entirely, and that work is already substantially landed (multiple cities merged the same night per the legacy-design-tools-shared-reader lane). Building a Factory-side atom writer for this rail would have silently overturned a standing active ruling. This is a stated, evidenced blocker satisfying the dispatch's own acceptance bar ('a real writer or a stated, evidenced blocker') without a code change.

whatRemainsOpen.item: setbackFrontFt architectural question: RULED, not implemented -- ruling recorded here so a successor is not re-deriving it
whatRemainsOpen.detail: This lane flagged (did not decide) whether parcel_record_cell.setbackFrontFt should carry an honest 'refused' state rather than staying 'unaccounted' indefinitely, given real setback service is now routed to Property Explorer's own runtime by an active 2026-09-05 operator ruling. doc-repo-26 RULED: YES, it should carry 'refused', citing the routing ruling as basis -- specifically 'refused', never 'absent-verified' and never 'not-applicable'. Reasoning, recorded verbatim in substance so it travels with the ruling rather than as an unexplained directive: (1) 'unaccounted' means nobody has established this cell's value, which is false here -- it HAS been established, just not by this ledger; recording a decision as an absence of information is a category error that every coverage figure computed over this rail then inherits. (2) 'unaccounted' is legitimate at rest but fatal at publish -- a rail that can never move off 'unaccounted' makes publish permanently impossible for every county, which forces an exception, and an exception is how one rail's fatal state becomes cover for every other rail sharing it. A 'refused' state with a reason citing the routing ruling keeps the gate honest and keeps the rail countable. (3) It must be 'refused' specifically: 'absent-verified' would falsely claim something looked and found nothing (nothing looked -- the parcel was never evaluated by this ledger), and 'not-applicable' would falsely claim the rail does not apply to these parcels (it does apply; it is served elsewhere by decision, not exempt). Implementation NOT performed by this lane -- this close is closing, per doc-repo-26's explicit instruction not to implement. Routed to doc-repo-26 for onward assignment.

lessons: LESSON: when a caller-supplied 'entity_id' field name matches a source table's own column name, do not assume the vendored function expects that literal column value passed through unchanged -- indexAtomsByPlaceKey's 'entity_id' is a generic join-key field name, and the correct usage here was aliasing a DIFFERENT jsonb path (body->>'parcelNodeId') into that field, not the atoms table's actual entity_id column (which carries a volatile suffix). Worth a test/note if another atom-reconciliation job is ever built against a different entity_type with a similarly-suffixed entity_id.

LESSON: a companion-rail vendored helper (companionRows/applyAtomPresenceToRecord) that can only emit kind:'value' is a real, load-bearing gap for any rail that has a legitimate absence state -- check for this before assuming an existing vendored ingest function is a complete solution for a new rail; the fix is job-level absence-handling code alongside the vendored call, not a vendored-code edit.
